LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 14.1.1 PRONUNCIATION AND INTONATION

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Strand 14
Topic 14.1: Listening and Speaking 14.1.1 Pronunciation and Intonation
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 14.1.1 Pronunciation and Intonation, part of Strand 14 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8 ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: when reading declarative and exclamatory sentences, 1. Why should we use the right intonation when speaking?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify silent consonant letters in words,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 14.1.1 Pronunciation and Intonation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. pronounce words with silent consonant letters in sentences,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 14.1.1 Pronunciation and Intonation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. use the correct intonation in declarative and exclamatory sentences,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 14.1.1 Pronunciation and Intonation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. acknowledge the importance of correct pronunciation and intonation in communication. • Search online and offline for words with the following silent consonant letters /r//h//k//g//p//t/and /b/ and practise the pronunciation of the given words, Control light intensity for learners who are sensitive to light while using the digital devices • Listen from the online dictionaries and tutorials for the correct articulation of the specified sounds, • Listen to the teacher or a recording of some sentences on sports and indicate whether a falling or rising intonation has been used, • Use correct intonation when reading declarative and exclamatory sentences, 1. Why should we use the right intonation when speaking? 2. What are some of the words with silent letters? 124 • practise reading words with silent letters in pairs and give feedback, • underline silent letters in words.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 14.1.1 Pronunciation and Intonation together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Self-efficacy is fostered as the learners identify what they find difficult as they endeavour to use correct intonation when

reading declarative and exclamatory sentences, and addressing the issue.

• Digital literacy is enhanced as the learners interact with recording of words on digital devices.

Values:
Social justice is promoted as learner practises reading words with silent letters in pairs and giving constructive feedback

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Effective communication is enriched as learners learn the correct pronunciation.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. identify silent consonant letters in words,
2. pronounce words with silent consonant letters in sentences,
3. use the correct intonation in declarative and exclamatory sentences,
4. acknowledge the importance of correct pronunciation and intonation in communication. • Search online and offline for words with the following silent consonant letters /r//h//k//g//p//t/and /b/ and practise the pronunciation of the given words, Control light intensity for learners who are sensitive to light while using the digital devices • Listen from the online dictionaries and tutorials for the correct articulation of the specified sounds, • Listen to the teacher or a recording of some sentences on sports and indicate whether a falling or rising intonation has been used, • Use correct intonation when reading declarative and exclamatory sentences, 1.
